title: Quantum annealing of the random transverse-field Ising model in one, two, and three dimensions
authors: István A. Kovács, Neil Shah, Róbert Juhász
abstract: Quantum annealing must be sufficiently slow to prevent defect formation. We study this problem in the random transverse-field Ising model via the adiabatic theorem to obtain the limiting rate at which defect formation can be avoided. Our approach based on the strong-disorder renormalization group (SDRG) technique views the annealing process as a gradual aggregation of strongly coupled clusters, giving access to the elementary events of error formation. We present a scaling theory of the statistics of these events in general dimensions and confront it to an extensive numerical analysis carried out in one, two, and three dimensions by an efficient implementation of the SDRG method. This approach is also validated by exact diagonalization in one dimension by means of the free-fermion technique. Our results consistently show a logarithmically slow decrease of the error density with the annealing time, characterized by the dimension-dependent critical exponents of the corresponding infinite-disorder fixed point of the model. Furthermore, we provide a map of individual events of potential defect formation in the excitation energy - control parameter plane, which may help in the design of optimal annealing paths.
summary: This work analyzes the adiabatic passage time required for quantum annealing of the random transverse-field Ising model. Using the Strong-Disorder Renormalization Group, the authors derive scaling theories showing that error density decreases logarithmically with time. This provides crucial insights for designing optimal, noise-resistant quantum annealing protocols.
main_problem: The paper determines the minimum annealing time required to prevent defect formation during quantum annealing in the random transverse-field Ising model.
main_result: The error density is shown to decrease logarithmically with annealing time, characterized by dimension-dependent critical exponents of the infinite-disorder fixed point.
method: The study employs the Strong-Disorder Renormalization Group (SDRG) technique combined with an analysis based on the adiabatic theorem.
model_or_system: The system is the random transverse-field Ising model (RTFIM) on $d$-dimensional lattices. The Hamiltonian is time-dependent, and the annealing process is analyzed via the adiabatic condition.
key_observables: Error density, Crossover Annealing Time ($	au_c$), and the gap ($\epsilon(s)$) between the ground and first excited state.
important_parameters: Dimension ($d=1, 2, 3$), annealing time ($	au$), and the critical exponents associated with the infinite-disorder fixed point.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the adiabatic theorem and uses the SDRG to model the process as a gradual aggregation of strongly coupled clusters.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the annealing-time threshold $Q(s)$ for the 1D RTFIM, showing the critical time $	au_c$.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theory using SDRG to model defect formation, derives scaling theories for error statistics in general dimensions, and validates the approach using exact diagonalization (free-fermion technique) in 1D.
why_interesting: The connection between quantum annealing dynamics, disorder physics (IDFP), and the calculation of critical time scales is highly relevant for understanding noise and robustness in quantum computation.
